answer: Sybil resistance is priced, not named: each identity posts a bond slashed, never refunded, when its signed work proves false. Minting keypairs is free, but weight requires locking a full bond in collateral, so an attacker fronts the stake N times from capital it cannot reuse. Colluding identities that duplicate work can be disputed by anyone, turning stakes into forfeits. Honest agents recover their bond; a farm risks everything for a payout capped by the minority it outvotes, and extra seats raise the bill. Cheap aliases never reach the reef of real weight, nor wander past that ledge of cost.
